narrative.overview: A quiet room with good instruments. The fleet works in the background and proposes; the operator decides. Most of the time nothing needs a person, and the screen says so plainly. When something does need a person, exactly one thing lights up: the decision, with everything needed to make it in view. Calm is the resting state, and colour is spent only on state and on the one action.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground, white panels, near-black ink; one blue for the action and links.
Status in three paired voices (ok, waiting, stopped): a dark ink on its own pale wash.
Exact things in JetBrains Mono; everything else in Inter.
Flat surfaces, 1px borders, 44px tap targets everywhere.
One badge in the whole UI: how many things wait for the operator.

rules.name: The Meaning Rule
rules.body: Colour is never decoration. Blue is the action, and the three status voices are state; a coloured element that is neither is a bug.

rules.name: The Paired Voice Rule
rules.body: Status text is always its dark ink on its own wash (for example wait-ink on wait-wash), never a coloured word on white or paper. Hue is never the only signal: every status also carries its word ("waiting for you", "failed").

rules.name: The Red Means Stop Rule
rules.body: stop-red fills a surface only when autonomy is frozen, or on the button that confirms a rejection. At rest the brakes are outlined, not red.

rules.name: The Exact Face Rule
rules.body: Anything the operator might copy, compare or type into a terminal is set in the Exact face; nothing else is.

rules.name: The Sixteen Rule
rules.body: Text fields use 16px text, so phones never zoom on focus.

rules.name: The No Sideways Scroll Rule
rules.body: At 360–430px no page scrolls sideways. Tables become stacked cards (each cell labelled with its column) below 640px; a wide diagram (the fleet workflow) stacks vertically.

rules.name: The Thumb Rule
rules.body: Below 640px the four navigation groups move to a fixed bottom bar, and the page reserves 104px at its foot so nothing hides under it.

rules.name: The Flat Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow on any surface. If something needs to stand out, give it a stronger border or its status band, not a lift.

dos: Do name the object on every action button ("Approve plan 4f1c…9e07", "Reject plan …").
Do set hashes, commands and ids in JetBrains Mono, and give the full value wherever it can be copied.
Do pair every status colour with its word.
Do check every page at 360, 390 and 1440px: no sideways scroll, 44px targets.
Do keep loosening actions (unfreeze, promote) behind a required reason; tightening actions (freeze, demote) act at once and can be undone.
donts: Don't use shadows, gradients or decorative colour.
Don't put a second badge anywhere; the only count is what waits for the operator.
Don't show red at rest: the brakes are quiet until used.
Don't show an approve button for a plan whose current content is not on screen.
Don't use fixed column counts for card grids, or tables that scroll sideways on a phone.
